item.title: Top 5 Methods to Plot in Multiple Subplots Using Matplotlib
item.description:
Creating effective visualizations is essential for data analysis and communication. One effective way to display multiple plots in a single figure is by using subplots in Matplotlib. Let’s dive into various methods of achieving this.

To start off, let’s consider a simple snippet that demonstrates how we can set up a figure with multiple subplots. The following code illustrates the process:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

## Create a figure with 2 rows and 2 columns of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(nrows=2, ncols=2)

## Each subplot can be accessed using axes[row, column]
axes[0, 0].plot(range(10), 'r')  # Top left: Red line
axes[1, 0].plot(range(10), 'b')  # Bottom left: Blue line
axes[0, 1].plot(range(10), 'g')  # Top right: Green line
axes[1, 1].plot(range(10), 'k')  # Bottom right: Black line

plt.show()

item.title: Top 7 Methods to Resolve Matplotlib Plotting Issues
item.description:
To effectively manage your plotting process in Matplotlib and avoid common pitfalls, you might find yourself grappling with how to tell Matplotlib that you are finished with a plot, especially when you want to start fresh for subsequent plots. Here, we will delve into **7 effective methods** that ensure your visualizations are rendered as you intend without overlap or confusion.

## First Approach: Using `figure()`

Creating a new figure is a fundamental way to ensure that each plot is independent. The code snippet below illustrates how invoking `figure()` prior to creating your plots can help:

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure()  # Create a new figure
x1 = [1, 10]
y1 = [30, 1000]
plt.loglog(x1, y1, basex=10, basey=10, ls="-")
plt.savefig("first.ps")

item.title: Top 7 Ways to Eliminate Gaps Between Subplots in Matplotlib
item.description:
To create tight and aesthetically pleasing visualizations in Matplotlib, managing the spacing between subplots is crucial. If you're struggling with unwanted gaps that disrupt the flow of your visuals, here are the **Top 7 Ways to Eliminate Gaps Between Subplots**. 

### Solution 1: Utilizing GridSpec for Full Control
You can master the spacing between subplots using [GridSpec](http://matplotlib.org/api/gridspec_api.html), which allows for precise control over subplots' layout. 

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.gridspec as gridspec

plt.figure(figsize=(4, 4))
gs = gridspec.GridSpec(4, 4)
gs.update(wspace=0.025, hspace=0.05)  # Control spacing between axes

for i in range(16):
    ax = plt.subplot(gs[i])
    plt.axis('on')
    ax.set_xticklabels([])
    ax.set_yticklabels([])
    ax.set_aspect('equal')

plt.show()
